caption:
A thermal anomaly on a pipeline route tells you heat is where heat shouldn't be. It does not tell you why.

Persistent thermal monitoring flags temperature signatures along a route — consistent with a tap, a flare, a fire, or routine maintenance. The signature alone does not distinguish between them. That call requires corroboration: optical confirmation on the next viable pass, ground reporting, or pattern against baseline.

The other limit is revisit, not resolution. A thermal pass samples the route at intervals — it does not watch it continuously. An anomaly that starts and clears between passes may never register. State what the system saw and when. Do not state more than that.
thread: A thermal anomaly on a pipeline route means heat is present where it shouldn't be. It does not mean you know the cause.
Tap, flare, fire, maintenance — all can produce a similar signature. Confirmation needs a second pass or ground reporting, not the thermal read alone.
Thermal monitoring samples a route at intervals. It does not watch it continuously. An anomaly that starts and ends between passes may not register.
Report what was seen and when. Grade the rest as assessed, not confirmed.

card.headline: Heat tells you where, not why
card.sub: A thermal anomaly flags a location. Cause — tap, flare, fire, maintenance — needs corroboration, not assumption.

rationale: Explains a distinct capability (thermal anomaly detection) while drawing a sharp, credible line around what it cannot determine alone, reinforcing periodic-sampling honesty without repeating prior angles.
